Every profiled product, plotted slow → fast from the review record. Dot rings carry the vein color; purple rings mark the blends and extracts. Positions are report-derived — the only vendor-published speed tags on the menu belong to 1692 and Horseman. Reading the spectrum: Slow = wind-down end · Mid = balanced middle · Fast = drive end. Tap a dot to jump to its card.

How the profiles were built. Bewitched Botanical does not publish a speed spectrum or effect grading of its own, so this guide builds both from the evidence: roughly 175 on-site customer reviews, graded strain by strain (see the evidence system). Every card shows the same six effects — Energy, Focus, Mood, Calm, Analgesia and Sleep — as percentages of that product's total reported profile. (The shop's own charts name two of them differently: what it calls clarity is scored here as Focus, and relief as Analgesia; Sleep is derived from each profile's calm-and-relief weight, and every profile is renormalized to 100 — derivations are printed, never hidden.)

Reading a card. The little pie in every card head opens that product's full effect chart. The bar under it is its place on the slow → fast spectrum. Badges on the head carry the vendor's own WooCommerce star rating; the formal reviews footnote sits with the master matrix.

Reading a Strain Card
  • Batch Tags — every card opens with the strain name and its line or batch tag. Bewitched works in small batches, and the vendor publishes exactly two lab batches — 16.06.888 and 16.4.111; the eight strains that carry one link straight to it in the Batch Index.
  • Effect Chips — six chips under each card head, one per effect. Thirty-six of the forty-one products carry this guide’s picker-record scores on five of them (Energy, Focus, Mood, Calm, Pain); Sleep is not scored in the picker record, so it reads 0 everywhere. The five format cards the record does not rank carry no chip row at all — a short note under the card head says why: they are formats and samplers, and the strains inside them are scored on their own cards (§44.22). The colored bar in each card head is the product’s place on the spectrum below.
  • Effect Pies — tap the small pie beside any strain’s name and a chart pops up with that strain’s own effect mix. Tap a big pie in the color panels above and you get that vein’s typical mix instead. Tap anywhere outside the chart to close it.
  • Spectrum — every profiled product’s slow → fast position is plotted on the map above and printed in the Master Matrix; positions are built from the review record, not the vendor’s labels.
  • Star Ratings — the stars on each card are the vendor’s own WooCommerce ratings; the formal reviews footnote sits with the master matrix.
  • Evidence — profiles are graded strain by strain from the review record, and cards say plainly where reports are thin — see the evidence notes.

Vein Color Feedback

How Every Claim in This Guide Is Graded.

Where the effects come from. Bewitched Botanical publishes almost no speed or effect grading of its own, so every profile here is built from the shop’s own review corpus — roughly 175 customer reviews, read in full for every product — cross-checked against the vendor’s recipe and copy. Where reports and vendor copy conflict, reports win, and the conflict is printed (Horseman’s tag, Enchanted Full Moon’s coffee, Moon Drops’ name). Effect percentages in each strain’s chart are normalized from those report-based ratings — nothing is invented to fill a gap.

The flags are part of the data. Two cards rest on vendor description alone because no community reports exist: 1692 (zero reviews) and Liminal Space (one content-free review). Scream Queen carries an era-split record — a 2024 phenomenon, a far weaker 2025 file — and both eras are printed. A handful of reviewers (one systematic voice above all) author a large share of the corpus, and duplicate reviews exist in it; averages run warm, so this guide weights detailed comparative reports over star counts.

On lab testing: unusually for a small shop, real COAs are published — Wonderland Labs certificates for six base strains under one batch number — but no blend of any kind has a published COA, and neither does the flagship Gold Bali. Full detail in the lab reference.

Stated plainly — the Reddit gap. This vendor’s customer base is visibly Reddit-recruited (one reviewer thanks “reddit people” for the referral), but Reddit itself could not be retrieved with the research tools available, and no Bewitched-specific Reddit threads surfaced in general search. Reddit sentiment is therefore an open gap in this guide — not silence, and not a consensus claimed either way. YouTube coverage exists only at hobbyist scale (Kratom Planet, Kr8tom Chai).

November 2026 — the record since this section was written. The vendor’s live catalog was re-checked end to end on November 2, 2026 — one new blend (Hocus Pocus) and a second COA batch (see the lab reference) are new since the original research.

Why reports vary. Effects vary significantly from person to person — hydration, sleep, medications and what you have eaten all move the experience, and the same bag can read differently on different days. That is why this guide prints distributions and disagreements instead of single verdicts, and why the batch-watch notes matter: with a one-woman, small-batch shop, the batch in your bag is part of the product.

The Company

One Woman, Small Batches, Honest Drift.

44Kratom products on the menu
2Published Wonderland batches
2.04%Top tested mitragynine
~175On-site reviews read in full
1Woman running the whole shop

The operation. Bewitched Botanical LLC is a one-woman shop: Candis, in the Tishomingo area of Oklahoma, blending personally since 2020. “Hi there, I’m Candis! I’m obsessed with all things natural, magical, and a little mysterious.” The catalog runs 43 kratom products (34 powders, 4 capsule products, 2 kilos, 2 sample packs, 1 potentiator) plus a “Mystical Goods” side shop. The community texture is real: blends are collaborations with customers and memorials to them, reviewers write like friends of the house, and purchases arrive fast with a free sample tucked in — “Candis is sweet and has the cutest packaging ever.”

How buying works. Charmingly manual: kilos, split kilos and sample-pack picks are specified in free-text checkout notes (“Tell me what you want in the notes section at checkout please!!!”). That is a genuine error surface — note an out-of-stock pick and it cannot be filled. Exchanges or store credit only, notice within 5 days, product unopened with heat seal intact; payment is due within 24 hours or the purchase auto-cancels. Shipments to West Virginia require ID verification. No shipping rate is published anywhere — cost appears at checkout only, and at least one reviewer has complained about it on the record.

Honest drift, itemized. A credible guide names these: the FAQ page is unfinished placeholder Latin, published and never completed. Pink Elf’s prose praises two strains that are not in its own recipe. Red Panji’s copy says “Unavailable” on a product you can purchase. The banner’s no-ship state list and the Shipping page’s list do not match. Gold Bali’s page still carries an old “18 years old” template block while the rest of the site enforces 21+. None of it is product fraud — it is a single operator’s website trailing her shelves. Practical consequence: treat recipes and stock status as best confirmed at checkout.

November 2026 check. The shop now lists 44 kratom products (35 powders — the new Hocus Pocus joined the classic line — 4 capsule products, 2 kilos, 2 sample packs and the turmeric potentiator) alongside the Mystical Goods side shop. The published contact points are support@bewitchedbotanical.com and 479-974-0843; the contact page's mailing address is PO Box 114, Tatums, OK 73487, and the shop's public business listing places it in the Tishomingo area. Candis's own summary, from her About page: "Hi there, I'm Candis! I'm obsessed with all things natural, magical, and a little mysterious."

Enhanced Blends — the Extract Line

The House Specialty: Leaf Plus Measured Extract.

Enhanced here means leaf plus measured extract — Diamond extracts, isolates, full-spectrum infusions up to a stated 30%. The ladder tops out at 1kg $89 (Horseman and Scream Queen $97): enhanced product at plain-leaf kilo money, a claim no other vendor in this series matches. No blend in this section has a published COA — the lab paper stops at the base strains — so these profiles rest entirely on the review record, graded hard.

🏆 Enhanced standouts: Enhanced 4078 Blend (the flagship by acclamation, 4.91 over 11 reviews); Wishbone (the clean-energy ceiling); Supernova (energy first, warm tail).

Key Compounds & Terms

TermWhat It Is
MitragynineKratom's dominant alkaloid — roughly 60% of the leaf's total alkaloid content and typically 0.5–2% or more of plain leaf by weight. A partial agonist at μ-opioid receptors: stimulant-like at low doses, sedating at higher ones. It is the number most COAs report.
7-Hydroxymitragynine (7-OH)A far more potent μ-opioid agonist than mitragynine. Fresh leaf holds only traces (about 0.01–0.04%) — most 7-OH forms after harvest by oxidation, and in the body when the liver enzyme CYP3A4 converts mitragynine. Noticeably elevated levels are a fingerprint of fortified or extract products.
SpeciociliatineKratom's second-most abundant alkaloid and a close chemical mirror of mitragynine (a diastereomer). In lab assays it is a stronger partial μ-opioid agonist than mitragynine itself, so its share of the mix helps set a lot's character.
SpeciogynineOne of kratom's major alkaloids. A smooth-muscle relaxant that acts as a competitive antagonist at opioid receptors in lab models — part of the leaf's built-in balancing chemistry.
PaynantheineAmong the three most abundant kratom alkaloids. In lab models it competes at μ- and κ-opioid receptors without activating them, quietly moderating the overall effect of the mix.
CorynantheidineA minor kratom alkaloid that functions as a μ-opioid antagonist in lab assays — one of the leaf's natural counterweights to its own agonists.
CYP3A4The liver enzyme chiefly responsible for converting mitragynine into 7-hydroxymitragynine. Its activity differs from person to person and shifts with other medications — one reason the same dose can hit two people very differently.

Buying, Shipping & Policies

How an Purchase Actually Works Here.

🚚 Shipping: Purchases are specified with unusual manual charm: kilos, split kilos and sample-pack picks are named in free-text checkout notes — write exactly what you want, and check it is in stock first, because an out-of-stock pick cannot be filled. Kratom purchases ship free (a candle-only purchase pays a flat $10). No shipping rate is published anywhere — cost appears at checkout only. No international shipping, and no shipping to military bases.

🚫 Where they don’t ship: Bewitched Botanical is an Oklahoma shop. Its Shipping page names six states it will not ship to — Alabama, Arkansas, Indiana, Rhode Island, Vermont and Wisconsin — plus a list of localities (San Diego & Oceanside, CA; Denver, Parker & Monument, CO; Sarasota County, FL; Alton, Glen Carbon, Edwardsville & Jerseyville, IL; Union County & Columbus City, MS; Franklin City, NH; Ontario, OR). The sitewide banner carries a different, broader list (adding Connecticut, Utah, Tennessee, Kansas, North Dakota and Massachusetts, among others). The two lists do not match — both are printed in full here, honestly labeled, rather than pretending they agree. Thirteen states require ID verification before shipping; West Virginia is one of them. Enhanced kratom cannot be shipped to Tennessee or Georgia. No international shipping, and no shipping to military bases.

↩️ Returns: Exchanges or store credit only: notice within 5 days of delivery, product unopened with the heat seal intact, return shipping on the buyer with tracking. Payment is due within 24 hours or the purchase auto-cancels.

⭐ How These Scores Were Earned
  • Product Quality — 4.6 / 5: the mean of the 34 rated products’ WooCommerce averages in this guide.
  • Value — 4.9 / 5: a $69 base kilo (6.9¢/g) — the cheapest kilo in any of the guides in this series; $89 enhanced kilos.
  • Service & Community — 4.6 / 5: collaborations, memorial blends, an active Discord, free samples, and fast free shipping on kratom purchases.
  • Catalog Depth — 4.4 / 5: 44 kratom products: 10 base, 12 classic, 14 enhanced, Moon Drops, capsules, kilos, samples.
  • Lab Transparency — 3.0 / 5: real COAs — two batches, 14 strain certificates — but six gallery values only, and no blend has ever been tested.
  • Consistency — 3.0 / 5: Scream Queen’s era split and the White Panji batch note are printed on their cards; small batches move.
  • Availability — 2.8 / 5: seven of ten base powders out of stock at the November 2026 check, and a 40-name retiring list announced for 2026.

Overall: 3.9 / 5. Bewitched is the value outlier of the vendor shelf: the cheapest kilos anywhere in these guides, an enhanced line priced like plain leaf, and a community warmth that is genuinely rare — held back by exactly the things its own record shows: thin lab coverage for a 35-powder menu, batch drift on its most famous blend, and a base line that is mostly out of stock while a long retiring list churns underneath. Buy the blends and the kilos with confidence; treat any single base strain's current batch as an open question.
